body: Maintainer's pick (2026-09-19) from the Tuppu Mark canvas: writing #4 of the six eBL lists for ṭuppu I — IM.DUB, 𒅎𒁾 (U+1214E U+1207E). DUB is the logogram "tablet", read with its Akkadian value ṭuppu; the IM before it is a determinative, "clay", written but not spoken. So the pair reads simply ṭuppu and literally writes "clay tablet", which is the About sentence. Attested for this exact word in both eBL's dictionary line (CDA: DUB; IM; IM.DUB) and its sign database (ebl.lmu.de/tools/dictionary/ṭuppu I). Shipped as a vector, never as text: nearly no phone or browser has a cuneiform font, so the Unicode characters would render as boxes. Outline from Noto Sans Cuneiform (OFL; embedding a glyph shape is permitted, the reserved-name clause only covers derivative fonts), composed with IM's advance, y flipped, origin at 0,0: 3419 x 1137 units, one path, commands M/L/H/V/Q/Z. Web: public/tuppu-cuneiform.svg, drawn tinted to the current text colour (a CSS mask over currentColor, since an cannot follow the theme). Android: drawable/ic_cuneiform_tuppu.xml, tinted onSurface. Same path in both. Placement, both clients: under the "Tuppu" heading on About, about 64dp tall, with the transliteration "ṭuppu" in small italics beneath it (one new string pair, identical in every locale, like the licence line). Prepared files: scratchpad cunei/tuppu-cuneiform.svg and ic_cuneiform_tuppu.xml.
title: The About screen shows the name in cuneiform: IM.DUB, read ṭuppu
